title: Finite ordered Postnikov towers for an arbitrary t-structure
statement:
Let $\mathcal U$ be a triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category] with a t-structure $t$ [def-weil-t-structure], heart $\mathcal H=\mathcal U^{\le0}\cap\mathcal U^{\ge0}$ and truncation functors $\tau^{\le q},\tau^{\ge q}$, which exist for every t-structure, bounded or not, together with the truncation triangles $\tau^{\le q}K\to K\to\tau^{\ge q+1}K\to\tau^{\le q}K[1]$, unique up to unique isomorphism [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles]. Write $H_t^q(K)=(\tau^{\ge q}\tau^{\le q}K)[q]\in\mathcal H$, regarded as an object of $\mathcal U$. For $a\in\mathbf Z$, $n\in\mathbf N$ and $K\in\mathcal U^{\ge a}\cap\mathcal U^{\le a+n-1}$, there exist objects $L_0,\ldots,L_n$ and distinguished triangles
$$L_j\longrightarrow L_{j+1}\longrightarrow H_t^{a+j}(K)[-a-j]\longrightarrow L_j[1]\qquad(0\le j<n),$$
with $L_0\cong0$, $L_n\cong K$ and $L_j\cong\tau^{\le a+j-1}K$ for every $0\le j\le n$. Thus the factors are the cohomology objects of this very $K$, in increasing degree, and there are exactly $n$ extension steps. For $n=0$ the assertion includes $K\cong0$ and no triangles. The t-structure need not be bounded or nondegenerate on all of $\mathcal U$; the actual t-bounds on $K$ are required. When $\mathcal U=D(\mathcal C)$ for an abelian category $\mathcal C$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with its standard t-structure [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], $H_t^q(K)\cong H^q(K)[0]$, so the displayed factors are $H^{a+j}(K)[0][-a-j]$.

source.place: Propositions 1.3.3 and 1.3.5, Theorem 1.3.6 and its derived-category example, pp. 29-32 (PDF pp. 30-33); finite ordered triangles as in 1.3.13, pp. 34-35. Derived-category specialization: Stacks derived.tex, Tag 08J5 (remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle).

proof.text: For 0 ≤ j ≤ n choose L_j = τ_{<a+j} K once and for all. The comparison truncLEIsoTruncLT identifies this with τ_{≤a+j-1} K. The zero-object clause of lem-sfb-upper-truncation-counit-calculus gives L_0 ≅ 0 from K ≥ a, and its invertible-counit clause gives L_n ≅ K from K ≤ a+n-1. The nested-counit clause is not needed: the next step uses the already constructed adjacent truncation triangle.

source.place: 1.3.3(i) and 1.3.4, pp. 29-30; original steps 1, 2, 4 and 5 extracted into the cited calculus leaf.

proof.text: For each $0\le j<n$ put $q=a+j$. Apply lem-sfb-adjacent-t-truncation-layer to $K,q$. Its first two vertices are $L_j,L_{j+1}$, and its third is $C_q=\tau^{\ge q}\tau^{\le q}K\in\mathcal U^{\ge q}\cap\mathcal U^{\le q}$. By the shift convention in def-weil-t-structure, $C_q[q]$ belongs to the heart; this is the stated $H_t^q(K)$. The inverse shifts identify $C_q\cong H_t^q(K)[-q]$. Substituting this isomorphism in the distinguished triangle is allowed by TR1 in def-weil-triangulated-category. The first arrows commute with the counits to this same $K$, as the layer node states.

source.place: 1.3.3-1.3.5, pp. 29-31; original step 3 supplied by the cited single-layer leaf, followed by shift cancellation.

proof.text: The vertices were chosen once, so these triangles share their adjacent vertices and are ordered by the increasing integers $a+j$. There are exactly $n$ integers $0\le j<n$. Step 1 gives the endpoints and the formula for every $L_j$. If $n=0$, the only vertex is $L_0=L_n$, the two endpoint isomorphisms give $K\cong0$, and there are no triangles. No argument used global boundedness or nondegeneracy.

source.place: Finite assembly of 1.3.3-1.3.5; compare 1.3.13, pp. 34-35. Original step 6.

proof.text: Let L = τ_{≤q}K and M = τ_{≥q}L for the standard derived t-structure. Its bounds put M in degrees [q,q], so Mathlib DerivedCategory.exists_iso_singleFunctor_obj_of_isGE_of_isLE gives an isomorphism e : M ≅ single_q(Y). The proved source-library lemmas DerivedCategory.isIso_homologyFunctor_map_truncLTι_app and isIso_homologyFunctor_map_truncGEπ_app identify H^q(L) with H^q(K) and H^q(M) with H^q(L). Composing these with H^q(e) and singleFunctorCompHomologyFunctorIso identifies Y with H^q(K). Apply single_0 to this coefficient isomorphism, and compose with e shifted by q and singleFunctors.shiftIso q 0 q, to obtain M[q] ≅ single_0(H^q(K)). Thus this is the cohomology of the original K, not merely an unspecified object of its heart. These are elementary compositions of the existing standard-t-structure and descended-cohomology comparison isomorphisms; no representative-level good-truncation or homotopy-colimit construction is required.

source.place: Tag 08J5 (remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle); explicit good truncation formulas, also BBD 1.3.2(i) and the example after 1.3.6

proof_origin.place: 1.3.3–1.3.6, pp. 29–32; finite assembly using Mathlib adjacent truncation triangles and endpoint calculus. The standard specialization uses the existing derived shifted-heart classification and cohomology comparison isomorphisms (Stacks Tag 08J5).

lean.statement: theorem exists_bounded_postnikov_tower {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Preadditive C] [HasZeroObject C] [HasShift C ℤ] [∀ m : ℤ, (shiftFunctor C m).Additive] [Pretriangulated C] [IsTriangulated C] (t : TStructure C) (a : ℤ) (n : ℕ) (K : C) [t.IsGE K a] [t.IsLE K (a + (n : ℤ) - 1)] : (∀ q : ℤ, t.heart (((t.truncGELE q q).obj K)⟦q⟧)) ∧ ∃ L : Fin (n + 1) → C, Nonempty (L 0 ≅ 0) ∧ Nonempty (L (Fin.last n) ≅ K) ∧ (∀ j : Fin (n + 1), Nonempty (L j ≅ (t.truncLE (a + (j : ℤ) - 1)).obj K)) ∧ ∃ (f : ∀ j : Fin n, L j.castSucc ⟶ L j.succ) (g : ∀ j : Fin n, L j.succ ⟶ (((t.truncGELE (a + (j : ℤ)) (a + (j : ℤ))).obj K)⟦a + (j : ℤ)⟧)⟦ -(a + (j : ℤ))⟧) (δ : ∀ j : Fin n, (((t.truncGELE (a + (j : ℤ)) (a + (j : ℤ))).obj K)⟦a + (j : ℤ)⟧)⟦ -(a + (j : ℤ))⟧ ⟶ (L j.castSucc)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧), ∀ j : Fin n, Triangle.mk (f j) (g j) (δ j) ∈ distTriang C
